## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Changes are needed: deleting the defaults file breaks its existing loader, port validation rejects a valid boundary value, and configuration errors disappear silently. Host normalization also has a documentation mismatch and an uncovered branch.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Deleting this file makes every call to `load_defaults()` raise `FileNotFoundError`; `app/startup.py:6` still reads it. Please retain the file or update its loader. — Existing defaults loading fails.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False` despite the documented inclusive range of 1–65535. Please change the upper comparison to `<=`. — Callers reject a valid TCP port.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — A missing config file or malformed JSON is caught by `except Exception` and returned as `{}` without any failure signal. Please propagate the error or provide an actionable diagnostic. — Callers cannot distinguish failed loading from a successfully loaded empty configuration.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring promises “returns None when h is empty,” but the empty-input branch executes `return ""`. Please align the documented contract and implementation. — Callers following the documentation cannot reliably recognize an empty host.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — No existing test exercises the trailing-dot branch, such as `normalize_host("Example.COM.") == "example.com"`; please add that assertion. — A regression that retains the trailing dot would pass the current tests.

## Strengths
- Added tests assert the millisecond conversion result and successful JSON configuration loading.
